subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: What user-visible context-overflow diagnostic facts may OpenClaw show by default, and how should session/channel identifiers be redacted?
rationale: Current source already has token, provider/model, budget, and session-key facts in logs/status, but exposing them in channel replies crosses UX and privacy policy boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
options.body: Use a shared formatter that includes model/provider, effective budget, measured or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted session/channel label while avoiding raw private identifiers.

options.title: Keep Details In Logs/Status
options.body: Keep channel replies short and generic, and direct users to /status, logs, or diagnostics for detailed token and session facts.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context UX
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers decide the broader context-visibility and warning design across /status, footers, compaction notices, and overflow errors.

recommendation.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Use a shared formatter that includes model/provider, effective budget, measured or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted session/channel label while avoiding raw private identifiers.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-main history on the affected runner/auto-reply paths and already framed the prior product-risk review for this issue.
